# StreamsPlayer command line

<!-- GENERATED by tools/Build-CliDoc.ps1 from docs/cli-commands.json. Do not edit by hand: change the manifest and run the tool. -->

Scripts, scheduled tasks, shortcuts, other programs and development agents can give StreamsPlayer commands. This page lists all 14 of them, command set version 1.0. It is generated from the manifest `docs/cli-commands.json`, which is the one source of truth and the same object `commands --json` prints.

## How to call

- **The running copy does the work.** A command is carried to the copy of StreamsPlayer that is already running, and the process you start waits for the answer and exits with the answer's exit code. A command never opens a dialog and waits for a person.
- **Two executables.** `StreamsPlayer.exe` is the window application. `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` is its console companion, for pipes and for scripts that read standard output; the `Executable` column below says which one serves each command. Both are installed side by side.
- **A window application has no console of its own.** The two channels a caller can always rely on are the exit code and the `--result <path>` file. To read the exit code of `StreamsPlayer.exe`, wait for it: `start /wait StreamsPlayer.exe ..` in cmd, `Start-Process -Wait -PassThru` in PowerShell. The examples below use that form.
- **List the commands.** `StreamsPlayerCli.exe commands [--json]`. It needs no running copy and opens no window; with `--json` it prints the manifest itself.
- **The risk setting.** A command whose risk is above `safe` is refused with exit `12` and reason `switch-off` until the person turns on **Let other programs ask STREAMS Player to work with my files, screen, clipboard or the network** in Settings. The setting is off by default and no command can change it. Where an exit code below says "the setting of rule 13", it means this setting.
- **Strict.** An unknown command, an unknown option, a missing value or a value of the wrong kind is refused with exit `10` and nothing is executed. Commands and options are matched without regard to case; values never are.
- **Reserved words.** The first word of a command line is a command, or one of the spellings listed under a command as also accepted; either one wins over a file of the same name. To reach such a file, give it as a path with a folder in it (`.\show`) or to the command that opens a file (`play --file`).

## Environment

| Variable | Selects the instance | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STREAMSPLAYER_DATA_DIRECTORY` | yes | A fully qualified folder. The process then keeps its state there and is an instance of its own (its lock and pipe names carry a profile hash), so commands reach only the copy that runs with the same value. |

## All commands

| Command | Risk | With nothing running | Executable | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`commands`](#commands) | `safe` | `oneshot` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Print the list of commands this product accepts. |
| [`version`](#version) | `safe` | `oneshot` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Print the product name, its version and the version of its command set. |
| [`status`](#status) | `safe` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Say whether StreamsPlayer is running and ready to take commands. |
| [`show`](#show) | `safe` | `start` | `StreamsPlayer.exe` | Bring the main window forward; started with no arguments the app opens (or comes forward) and plays nothing. |
| [`quit`](#quit) | `safe` | `oneshot` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Close the running StreamsPlayer cleanly; with none running there is nothing to do. |
| [`play`](#play) | `safe` | `start` | `StreamsPlayer.exe` | Play a saved channel, a stream address or a StreamsPlayer broadcast resource file. |
| [`playback stop`](#playback-stop) | `safe` | `oneshot` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Stop the playing stream (all of them with --all); nothing playing is already the goal. |
| [`playback pause`](#playback-pause) | `safe` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Pause the playing radio (the audio session). Video windows have no pause. |
| [`playback resume`](#playback-resume) | `safe` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Resume the paused radio. |
| [`playback status`](#playback-status) | `reads-user-data` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | List what plays now: kind, channel, title, state and whether it is being recorded. |
| [`volume set`](#volume-set) | `safe` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Set the volume of the radio or of the video players, and mute or unmute video. |
| [`record start`](#record-start) | `writes-user-data` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Start recording a playing stream into a folder the caller names; nothing is ever written anywhere else. |
| [`record stop`](#record-stop) | `writes-user-data` | `refuse` | `StreamsPlayerCli.exe` | Finish the recording and report the file, its size and its length. |
| [`channel add`](#channel-add) | `safe` | `start` | `StreamsPlayer.exe` | Add a stream address to the user's own list (a Manual channel that a catalog refresh never touches). |

Risk: `safe` changes only the application's own state or window and reads nothing of yours; `reads-user-data` puts something of yours into the answer or a file you name; `writes-user-data` creates or changes files or settings outside the application's own data folder; `leaves-machine` sends anything off this PC. Only `safe` commands work while the setting above is off.

With nothing running: `start` makes the process the running copy and then runs the command; `oneshot` does the work and exits without leaving a window or tray icon; `refuse` answers exit `11` (reason `not-running`).

```text

```

Risk `safe`; with nothing running `oneshot`; waits for `done` up to 5 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; done by the process you start, never carried to a running copy; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | false | Print the manifest itself as JSON. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | printed |

```powershell
StreamsPlayerCli.exe commands --json | ConvertFrom-Json
```

Expected: the manifest as an object; exit 0, no window opens and no running copy is needed.

```text

```

Risk `safe`; with nothing running `refuse`; waits for `done` up to 2 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | false | Print the response line itself. |

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | string | the running copy's version |
| `pid` | int | its process id |
| `acceptsRestrictedCommands` | bool | whether the setting that lets other programs ask for more than the safe commands is on |
| `activeSessions` | int | how many streams play now (a count only) |

### play

Play a saved channel, a stream address or a StreamsPlayer broadcast resource file.

```text
StreamsPlayer.exe play (--id <guid> [--url <address> | --url-file <path>] | --url <address> | --url-file <path> | --file <path.spres>) [--background] [--json] [--result <path>]
```

Risk `safe`; with nothing running `start`; waits for `done` up to 30 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayer.exe`; since 1.0.

Also accepted, as shipped spellings of this command:

- `--url {url}` (shipped before this command line existed; {url} is read as `--url`)
- `--id {id}` (shipped before this command line existed; {id} is read as `--id`)
- `--id {id} --url {url}` (shipped before this command line existed; {id} is read as `--id`; {url} is read as `--url`)
- `{file}` (shipped before this command line existed; {file} is read as `--file`)

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--id` | guid | no | - | A saved channel's id. Exactly one target is required: --id (optionally with --url or --url-file), --url, --url-file, or --file. |
| `--url` | string | no | - | A stream address (http, https or rtsp). With --id it is the fallback that finds the channel again after a catalog refresh replaced its row. May carry a credential; never logged or returned. Sensitive: never written to a log line, an answer or a message; also taken from --url-file. |
| `--url-file` | path | no | - | A file whose one UTF-8 line is the stream address, for an address that carries a credential and must stay out of the command line and the shell history. Taken in place of --url; a relative path is taken from the caller's working folder. |
| `--file` | path | no | - | A .spres broadcast resource document: it is imported, then played. |
| `--background` | bool | no | false | Do not bring the window forward. |
| `--json` | bool | no | false | Print the response line itself. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as JSON. |

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channelId` | guid | the channel that plays |
| `title` | string | its title |
| `kind` | enum | audio or video |
| `state` | enum | playing |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | playing: the first sound or picture arrived, or the stream already played |
| `1` | the stream did not open (reason stream-failed) |
| `2` | no sound or picture within the bound; the app may still be trying |
| `10` | no target, two targets, an address that is not http, https or rtsp, an empty --url-file, or an unreadable .spres |
| `11` | busy, --id is not in the catalog and no --url was given, or the file of --url-file does not exist (reason target-missing) |
| `12` | the broadcast needs a link password that is not stored on this PC (reason needs-person); the command never asks for it |
| `14` | the file of --url-file cannot be read (reason io-error) |
| `15` | the stream's host could not be reached |

```cmd
start /wait StreamsPlayer.exe play --url https://example.org/live.mp3 --background
```

Expected: exit 0 once the radio is audible.

```powershell
(Start-Process .\StreamsPlayer.exe -ArgumentList 'play','--id','<channel-guid>' -Wait -PassThru).ExitCode
```

Expected: 0 while the saved channel plays.

```powershell
(Start-Process .\StreamsPlayer.exe -ArgumentList 'play','--url-file','.\camera-address.txt' -Wait -PassThru).ExitCode
```

Expected: 0 once the stream of the address on the first line of the file plays; the address never appears on the command line or in the log.

### playback stop

Stop the playing stream (all of them with --all); nothing playing is already the goal.

```text
StreamsPlayerCli.exe playback stop [--id <guid> | --all] [--result <path>]
```

Risk `safe`; with nothing running `oneshot`; waits for `done` up to 10 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--id` | guid | no | - | The channel to stop. Required (or --all) when more than one stream plays. |
| `--all` | bool | no | false | Stop every playing stream. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as JSON. |

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stopped` | int | how many sessions were stopped |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | stopped, or nothing was playing |
| `10` | several streams play and neither --id nor --all was given, or both were |
| `11` | busy (a modal dialog is open) |

```cmd
StreamsPlayerCli.exe playback stop --all
```

Expected: exit 0 (errorlevel 0).

### playback status

List what plays now: kind, channel, title, state and whether it is being recorded.

```text
StreamsPlayerCli.exe playback status [--json] [--result <path>]
```

Risk `reads-user-data`; with nothing running `refuse`; waits for `done` up to 5 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | bool | no | false | Print the response line itself. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as JSON. |

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions` | array | one object per open stream: kind (audio or video), channelId, title, state (playing, paused, buffering, failed), recording (bool). The stream address is never included. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | listed (an empty list when nothing plays) |
| `1` | the list is over the 64 KiB bound of an answer (reason response-too-large) |
| `11` | not running, or busy |
| `12` | the setting of rule 13 is off |

```powershell
(StreamsPlayerCli.exe playback status --json | ConvertFrom-Json).data.sessions
```

Expected: one object per open stream while the setting is on.

### volume set

Set the volume of the radio or of the video players, and mute or unmute video.

```text
StreamsPlayerCli.exe volume set --level <0-100> [--target audio|video] [--muted <true|false>]
```

Risk `safe`; with nothing running `refuse`; waits for `done` up to 5 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--level` | int | yes | - | 0 to 100. |
| `--target` | enum: audio, video | no | audio | Which volume: the radio's or the video players'. |
| `--muted` | bool | no | - | Mute or unmute; accepted for video only. |

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | int | the volume now in force |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | set |
| `10` | level outside 0-100, or --muted with the audio target |
| `11` | not running, or busy |

```cmd

```

Expected: exit 0 (errorlevel 0).

### record start

Start recording a playing stream into a folder the caller names; nothing is ever written anywhere else.

```text
StreamsPlayerCli.exe record start --out <folder> [--id <guid>] [--result <path>]
```

Risk `writes-user-data`; with nothing running `refuse`; waits for `done` up to 15 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--out` | path | yes | - | The folder the recording is written into: an existing folder, which this command never creates. A relative path is taken from the caller's working folder. The file name inside it is the product's own (CAPTURE-OUTPUT: kind, prefix, name) and an existing file is never replaced. |
| `--id` | guid | no | - | The playing channel to record; optional when exactly one stream is open. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as JSON. |

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | path | the folder the recording is written into, as the caller named it, in full |
| `kind` | enum | audio or video |
| `file` | path | the file being written, inside the folder; given for a radio recording only - a video file is named when it ends, see record stop |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | recording: the first recorded data was seen (a second start on the same stream into the same folder answers the same recording) |
| `1` | the stream cannot be recorded (reason not-recordable: a StreamsPlayer broadcast, a format a byte copy cannot record) or the recording could not start (error, stream-failed) |
| `2` | no recorded data was seen within the bound; the recording may still be starting - run the command again, or record stop |
| `10` | no --out, a doubled --out or --id, several streams open and no --id, or --out is a file and not a folder |
| `11` | not running, busy, no stream is open or the named one is not, the radio is paused or the stream failed, the stream is already recorded into another folder, or the folder of --out does not exist (reason target-missing) |
| `12` | the setting of rule 13 is off |
| `13` | no space for the recording (reason no-space) |
| `14` | the folder of --out cannot be written (reason io-error) |

```powershell
StreamsPlayerCli.exe record start --out D:\Recordings; $LASTEXITCODE
```

Expected: 0 while a stream plays and the setting is on.

### record stop

Finish the recording and report the file, its size and its length.

```text
StreamsPlayerCli.exe record stop [--id <guid>] [--result <path>]
```

Risk `writes-user-data`; with nothing running `refuse`; waits for `done` up to 30 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayerCli.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--id` | guid | no | - | The channel being recorded; optional when exactly one recording runs. |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as JSON. |

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | path | the finished file in the folder of record start; the first one when parts is above 1 |
| `bytes` | int | its size in bytes, all parts together |
| `seconds` | int | the recorded length, all parts together |
| `parts` | int | how many files the recording is in: more than 1 only when the stream dropped and was opened again while recording |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | the file is finished |
| `1` | the recording ended with nothing saved |
| `2` | finishing has not ended within the bound; the file may still be completing |
| `10` | a doubled --id, or several recordings run and no --id |
| `11` | not running, busy, nothing is being recorded or the named stream is not, or the recording is already being finished |
| `12` | the setting of rule 13 is off |
| `13` | no space to finish the recording (reason no-space) |
| `14` | the file could not be written or moved into the folder (reason io-error) |

```powershell
StreamsPlayerCli.exe record stop --result C:\temp\rec.json; Get-Content C:\temp\rec.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
```

Expected: an object with file, bytes, seconds and parts.

### channel add

Add a stream address to the user's own list (a Manual channel that a catalog refresh never touches).

```text
StreamsPlayer.exe channel add (--url <address> | --url-file <path>) [--title <text>] [--collection <name>] [--result <path>]
```

Risk `safe`; with nothing running `start`; waits for `done` up to 10 s; never waits for a person; safe to run again; executable `StreamsPlayer.exe`; since 1.0.

| Option | Kind | Required | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--url` | string | no | - | A stream address (http, https or rtsp). May carry a credential; never logged or returned. Exactly one of --url and --url-file is required. Sensitive: never written to a log line, an answer or a message; also taken from --url-file. |
| `--url-file` | path | no | - | A file whose one UTF-8 line is the stream address, for an address that carries a credential and must stay out of the command line and the shell history. A relative path is taken from the caller's working folder. |
| `--title` | string | no | - | The channel's title; the address's host when absent. |
| `--collection` | string | no | - | An existing collection to put the channel in (never created by this command). |
| `--result` | path | no | - | Where to write the response data as JSON. |

Exactly one of `--url` or `--url-file` is given.

Returns, in the `data` member of the answer and in the `--result` file:

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channelId` | guid | the new channel's id, or the existing one |
| `created` | bool | false when the address was already in the list |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | added, or already there |
| `10` | no address, both --url and --url-file, an empty --url-file, an address that is not http, https or rtsp, or a repeated option |
| `11` | busy (a catalog refresh or a dialog is open), --collection names no collection, or the file of --url-file does not exist (reason target-missing) |
| `14` | the catalog could not be saved, or the file of --url-file cannot be read (reason io-error) |

```powershell
Start-Process .\StreamsPlayer.exe -ArgumentList 'channel','add','--url','https://example.org/live.mp3','--title','Example' -Wait
```

Expected: exit 0; the channel is in My streams.
